According to the latest report from Counterpoint Research, Apple iPhone shipments grew 3% year-on-year and reached a record-high 20% share of global smartphone shipments, despite an industry-wide downturn. Here's a detailed look.

The Second Quarter's Lowest Level Since 2013

Counterpoint Research said that in the second quarter of 2026, Samsung led the global smartphone market with a 24% shipment share, followed by Apple at 20% (a record high for the quarter), Xiaomi at 12%, OPPO at 11%, and vivo at 8%.

Compared with the same period last year, Samsung's share rose by 4 percentage points, Apple's by 3 percentage points, and vivo's by 1 percentage point, while Xiaomi's dropped by 2 percentage points and OPPO's by 1 percentage point. The combined share of other manufacturers fell from 28% to 26%.

Counterpoint noted that Samsung returned to the top of the global smartphone sell-in rankings in the second quarter of 2026, after Apple had taken the lead in the first quarter on the back of strong demand for the iPhone 17.

As for the second quarter of 2026, although Apple was the only major OEM that did not raise prices, Samsung benefited from strong demand for the Galaxy S26 series, improved product supply, and a more aggressive promotional strategy, enabling it to grow at a faster pace.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects "global smartphone shipments for the full year to decline by around 14%, with the global memory shortage projected to persist into 2027." The firm noted that manufacturers will continue to cut low-margin models, adjust storage configurations, and rely more heavily on refurbished and previous-generation devices until supply conditions improve.
